events.title: Baptism
events.place: Parish of San Tommaso d'Aquino, San Mango d'Aquino
events.description: Baptized the day after her birth as Maria Philumena, daughter of Leopoldo Ferlaino and Josepha (Giuseppina) Fiorillo; godmother Saveria Sacco.

bioAdditions: Helen was baptized in the parish of San Tommaso d'Aquino at San Mango d'Aquino on 9 October 1894, the day after her birth, as Maria Philumena (Filomena), daughter of Leopoldo Ferlaino and Josepha Fiorillo. The godmother was Saveria Sacco (S1). I read the register entry myself on the volunteer-photographed page (S2). She is the only child of this couple anywhere in the San Mango baptism registers. Her 1894 birth matches her age in the 1920 census (25) and her emigration with her mother in 1900. 'Helen' was evidently the name she used in America. The 'Filomena Ferlaino' whom the site and FamilySearch list as Frank Cognetti's other wife is almost certainly the same woman. The Pennsylvania death-certificate index records Helen Cognetti, aged 69, dying in South Abington Township, Lackawanna County, on 14 March 1965 (certificate file 027518; residence code 35001 = Scranton) (S3). An age of 69 fits a birth in late 1894 or 1895. The baptism resolves the Ferlaino-versus-Farina question: Helen was born a Ferlaino, and 'Farino/Farina' is the US clerks' spelling.

conflicts.assessment: Baptism is a primary record; adopt 8 Oct 1894.

conflicts.siteValue: Separate person Filomena Ferlaino (I282695503686), also wife of Frank Cognetti
conflicts.assessment: Probable: only one daughter of Leopoldo and Giuseppina was baptized in San Mango, in 1894. Merge, keeping Helen as the display name.

confidenceRecommendation.justification: Baptism names Leopoldo Ferlaino and Giuseppina Fiorillo; the birth date fits the US census; the widowed mother Josephine headed the household in 1920; US clerks wrote Farino. Taken together, the link to John is documented. Only her death certificate or marriage license would add a US record naming Ferlaino outright.
